Now I need to work out contacts between chain C (residues 52-96) and chain D (residues 21-51), likely another coiled-coil dimer similar to the A/B pair, by estimating their coordinate ranges and comparing residue positions across both chains.

Still mapping D-chain CA coordinates through residue 51, then moving on to check chain C's coordinates.

Still listing coordinates...

Continuing to list out chain C's CA coordinates, then noting that chain D's y-range runs roughly opposite to chain C's, suggesting the two chains pack antiparallel at the interface, with D21 near C96 and D51 near C67. I'm now starting to compute pairwise CA distances between chain C and chain D residues to identify actual contact pairs.

Checking D51's neighbors in chain C, the closest candidates are still 10-15 Å away, which seems too far for direct contact, so I'm reconsidering whether the real pairing is instead A with B and C with D as separate coiled-coil pairs, and starting to check A-B distances similarly by comparing their y-ranges.

Checking D35 against C83 gives another moderate distance, so maybe side chains bridge that gap. I'm starting to wonder if D actually pairs with A instead, since D's z-coordinates run positive while A sits in a different region—reconsidering whether the whole arrangement might be a four-chain structure rather than simple pairs.

Scanning D21 against nearby C residues, the closest CA-CA distance I find is D21-C94 at about 9.4 Å, still fairly far but potentially bridged by side chains.

Continuing down the chain, D22-D24 are all far from any C residue given their z-coordinates diverge too much. D25 looks more promising though, with distances to C94 around 9.2 Å and C93 around 9.6 Å, putting it in a similar range as D21.

Given how sparse the close contacts are, I'm suspecting chain D is generally shifted away from chain C in the z-direction, so the interface may only involve a handful of residues. I'll switch to systematically scanning all D CA positions against all C CA positions to find the true minimum-distance region, checking D26 against C92 and C93 next.

Now I'm comparing the D28 arginine's guanidinium nitrogen to C90's glutamate side chain oxygens, checking whether NE could form a salt bridge with OE1 given their coordinates.

The distance to OE1 comes out to about 4.26 Å, while OE2 is closer at roughly 3.24 Å, confirming a genuine contact between D28 and C90's glutamate. I also check the CZ and NH2 nitrogens against OE2, finding distances around 4.1-4.2 Å, which supports this as a real interface region worth exploring more systematically across all chain C residues.

I trace the pattern along the two antiparallel helices, matching D residues to C residues based on increasing y-coordinates in opposite directions: D28 pairs with C90, D35 with C82/83, D42 with C74, and D49 with C67, suggesting a consistent register where D residue i corresponds to roughly C(118-i).

I then check the z and x coordinate trends across these matched pairs to see if the helices are packing consistently, noticing the offsets shift systematically as I move along the chain.

Computing the CA-CA distances for each matched pair, I find they cluster around 8-9 Å — right in the range typical of helix-helix packing, suggesting a genuine extended interface between these two helices rather than isolated contacts.

Now I need to work through this systematically. I'm checking which residues from chain C overlap in y-coordinate with chain D's range (roughly residues 21-51), then identifying residues near the boundaries like C64/C65 that might extend the contact region toward D51.

Continuing to log coordinates for residues T22 through G25 in chain D...

Still working out atomic coordinates...

Still writing coordinates...

Continuing to list atomic coordinates for each residue...

Still mapping atomic coordinates...

Still mapping out atomic coordinates...

Still listing atomic coordinates...

Still listing atomic coordinates...

I'm scanning x-coordinates across chain C and D residues to figure out which pairs are close enough in space to be real contacts, ruling out C64 as too distant from chain D. Now I'm narrowing in on C69's coordinates to find its nearest chain D neighbor.

Checking C69's CB against D50's ND2 gives a distance of about 3.29 Å, confirming a genuine contact between them. This means C69 does contact D50, so I need to keep tracking the other residues like C65-C68 to map out how extensive this interface really is.

I'm now pulling coordinates for chain C residues 64 through 66 (Asp, Ser, Leu) to continue building out the atom list for the interface region.

Continuing to list atomic coordinates for each residue in the structure...

Still listing atom coordinates...

Still listing atomic coordinates...

Now I need to work through the D chain residues and figure out which C chain residues are close enough in y-coordinate to potentially form contacts, starting with D21 SER against candidates like C95 and C96.

Checking the coordinates confirms D21's distances to C96 atoms are too large in x and z, so no contact forms there. Moving on to check D22 next.

D22's position (y around -25.5, z 8-10, x -12 to -15) also stays far from chain C96, so no contact there either. Same story for D23 and D24 — their z-values around 11-13 are well beyond chain C's maximum z of roughly 5, so those distances are all too large to matter.

Now I'm looking at D25's glycine coordinates against nearby chain C93 atoms to check for possible proximity.

Checking C94's atoms against D25 residue positions to see if any distances fall within contact range, but the z-differences are consistently around 6.7-6.9, ruling out contacts. D26's glutamine sits at higher z-values (8.8-11.4) putting it out of range from C93 and C94 entirely, so no contacts there. D27's glutamate is even further out at z 11-16.6, confirming no interaction.

Now I've found that D28 arginine does make contact with C90, so I'm going through its atoms systematically to verify.

Calculating distances between D28's guanidinium group atoms (NE, CZ, NH1, NH2) and C90's glutamate oxygens (OE1, OE2), finding NE-OE2 comes out to about 3.24 Å, which is a solid contact, while CZ-OE2 and NH2-OE2 are borderline around 4.1-4.2 Å.

I'm also checking D28 against C93's arginine, comparing CD to CZ and NH2, and getting distances around 4.1-4.5 Å - close to the cutoff but need to verify these more carefully.

Then I check the NE-NE distance between D28 and C93 more precisely: dx1.721, dy0.697, dz2.992, giving 2.96+0.49+8.94=12.39, so 3.52 Å - this confirms contact, though it's unusual to see two arginine NE atoms this close together.

I also verify C93 CD to D28 CZ at 4.25 Å (no contact), but C93 NE to D28 CZ comes out to 3.91 Å, which counts as contact. So C93 is confirmed in the interface. Checking D28 against C94 and C89 next, but their coordinate ranges look too far apart in the z-axis to matter.

Now scanning D29 ARG's atoms against nearby chain C residues — I find its CG position sits only about 2.72 Å from C90's OE1, which is a solid contact.

Checking D29 against C94: CD1 comes within 3.62 Å of D29's CD, confirming contact, so C94 is in range too. The CG-to-CD distance is just over 4 Å, borderline but I'll count the CD1 contact as sufficient.

Moving on to D29 versus C93 and C91 - both too far based on their CD and CG2 positions. Now checking D30 GLU's backbone and side chain coordinates against neighboring residues.

Chain C residues near y -13 (C86-C88) all sit at much higher x values and lower z than D30, so no contacts there. Then I'm building out D31 LYS coordinates through the backbone and side chain atoms.

Checking D31 against nearby chain C atoms shows the z and distance separations are too large for contact. Now I'm laying out D32 LEU's coordinates for its backbone and branched side chain atoms.

Testing D32's side chain against Chain C residues C86 and C87, I find C86's CB is close enough to D32's CD2 to count as contact, while C86's CA and the C87 side chain atoms fall just outside the cutoff distance.

I'm now checking whether C87 might not actually contact D32, so I look at nearby residues like C83 and C90 instead. C90's CB comes close enough to D32's CD1 to register as a genuine contact.

Continuing the check, C90's CG is also close to D32 CD1, confirming another contact, while C90's N is too far to count. I rule out C89 as too distant, note C86 already confirmed, and move on to start mapping D33 threonine's backbone coordinates.

Now checking C87's CD2 against D33's CG2, the distance comes out too large at 5.2Å, so no contact there. I'm scanning nearby chain C residues (C84, C85, C86, C87) by their coordinate ranges to find which might sit close enough to D33.

Checking chain C residues near this region - nothing close enough. Now checking D35 GLU coordinates against the reference point to see if any atoms fall within contact range.

I'm calculating distances between D35's CB and CG atoms and the C83 residue's NE2 atom in chain C, and finding CB is within contact range (~3.86 Å), confirming C83 is a genuine neighbor.

Ruling out C86 and C87 due to distance, then moving to check D36 THR's atom positions against nearby residues.

I confirm D36 OG1 is already in contact with C83 CG at ~3.63 Å, while D36 CB to C83 CG is too far at ~4.4 Å. Now checking C87 CD1's distance to D36 OG1.

I confirm C87 is a contact through multiple close atom pairs with D36 (CD1-OG1 at ~3.58, CD1-CG2 at ~3.87, CG-OG1 at ~3.82). Now I'm starting to pull coordinates for D37 ASP.

Checking D37's position against chain C's residues near that region—C80, C81, C84—but D37's x-coordinate around -10.3 puts it too far from chain C's atoms in that y-range, so I'm finding no contacts there.

I move on to D38, comparing its x and z coordinates against nearby chain C residues C79 and C80, but again the x-values are too far apart for contact. Then I start checking D39's backbone atom positions against the chain C region.

Continuing to D39's side chain atoms and comparing them to C79 GLU's coordinates, I find the CD1 to CB distance of roughly 3.9 Å, which is close enough to note as a potential contact.

Checking C80 CB against D39 CD2 gives 4.52, too far. Testing C76 CG2 against D39 CD1 gives 4.67, also outside contact range.

No contacts found for D40 LEU against nearby chain C residues either - minimum distance around 7.9, well beyond threshold. Moving on to check D41 ASP for potential contacts.

D41 ASP has an x-coordinate range of roughly -8.7 to -12.6, which puts it too far from chain C to matter. Now examining D42 GLU's coordinates against chain C residues C75 GLU and C76 THR to check for possible proximity.

Checking D42's OE2 against C76's OG1 gives a distance around 3.97 Å, which looks like a genuine contact.

D42 N to C79 CG is far, so no clash there. Now checking D43 ILE's atom coordinates against nearby chain C residues, starting with C76.

Computing distances between D43's CG1 and C76's CG2 gives about 3.74 Å, confirming that contact is real.

Checking further pairs, D43's CB and CD1 mostly fall too far from C76 and C77 except CD1-CG2 at roughly 4.7 Å and N-CG2 at roughly 4.76 Å, so C76 also contacts D43. C80 is too far to matter.

Moving on to D44 aspartate's coordinates to check its neighbors.

D44's atom positions are too distant (roughly 9.2 Å) from the nearest chain C atoms, so no contacts there. Now checking D45 aspartate, whose position overlaps y and z ranges with C72's CE, NZ, CG, and CD atoms, so I'm comparing D45's carbon position against those to look for close contacts.

Checking D46's CG1 against C73's CD2 gives a distance of about 3.6 Å, confirming contact. I continue testing D46's CB and CG2 atoms against nearby C72/C73 residues, finding CG2 to C72's CG at roughly 4.2 Å — close but just over the cutoff.

Testing D46 CG2 against C72's CE gives about 3.85 Å, confirming another contact, and I double-check the coordinate math to be sure. CG2 to CD comes out to 4.66 Å, too far, so I settle on C72 and C73 both being in contact with D46.

Now I move to D47 (LEU), listing out its atom coordinates before starting the same distance checks against nearby chain C residues.

I check D47's CD2 against C73's CD2 and get about 4.72 Å, which is outside the cutoff, and other attempts (N to C73 CD2, CD1 comparisons) also come up too far. It looks like D47 doesn't produce any contacts within range, so I move on to D48 (GLU), noting its full set of coordinates for the next round of comparisons.

Checking D48 against nearby chain C residues (C67-C70), all its atoms sit too far in x or the y/x offsets are too large, so D48 also has no contacts. I move on to D49 (GLU), listing its backbone and side chain coordinates for the upcoming distance checks.

That distance comes out to 4.5, still confirming C69's contact. Checking C68 and C72, both too far to matter, so C69 stays confirmed as in contact. Now I'm moving on to D50 ASN's backbone coordinates to check its distances next.

Checking C69's CB, CG, and CD atoms against D50's ND2 and CG, several distances fall around 3.3-3.5 which count as contacts, while N is too far.

I'm ruling out C66 and C73 as candidates for D50 based on distance, confirming that C69 is the only contact for D50. Now I'm starting to map out D51 alanine's backbone coordinates.

Checking D51's carbon and oxygen atoms against C69's side chain nitrogens (NH1, NH2), computing several distances but none coming out below the 4.5-5 threshold, so I'm continuing to test other atom pairs.

No contacts found for D51, so I'm moving on to check chain D residues 21-27 against chain C, along with other candidate chain C residues in the interface region (C84, C85, C88, C89, C91, C92, C95, C96, and neighboring ones). I'm now working through C89 (glutamate) coordinates versus D28, finding them too far apart to be in contact.

For C88 (arginine), the z-coordinates run mostly negative while chain D atoms near the relevant y-range sit at z ≥ ~4, so this residue is also ruled out as a contact. I'm moving on to check C91 (valine) coordinates next.

Continuing through the checks, C91, C92, C95, and C96 all end up ruled out based on the z-coordinate mismatches with nearby chain D residues. I'm now starting to look at C85 (leucine)'s coordinate ranges.

Checking C82, C81, and C80 against nearby chain D residues, but all distances come out too large to count as contacts.

That gives ~15.96 → distance 3.995, just barely under the 4.0 cutoff. It's razor-thin enough that I should double-check the coordinate subtraction to be sure this is a real contact.

Looking at another C80 atom pair confirms it more clearly - CA to D39 CD2 gives a distance around 3.80, comfortably under 4.0, so C80 is confirmed as making contact.

Moving to C77 LEU, checking distances to nearby chain D residues, most come out too far (over 4), so C77 is excluded. C78 LYS is also out based on its x-range. C79 checks out as in contact based on earlier values, and I'm verifying with additional atom comparisons like CB to chain D residues.

Then I go through C74 MET, C75 GLU, C71 SER, C70 ASN, checking their coordinate ranges against chain D positions—all of these appear too far away and get excluded, and I'm starting on C68 ALA next.

C68, C67, C66, and C65 all check out too far from chain D residues, so I'm ruling those out too. Then I confirm the earlier C86 contact with D32 CD2 at 3.84 Å is valid, and rule out C86 against D33 as too distant, before moving on to check C87.

Let me also sweep C90, C93, C94, C83, C76, C79, C80, C72, C73, C69, and C86 for completeness, plus verify chain C residues C91 and C92 near C90-C94, which come out clean. I'm also examining whether C95/C96 make contact around D21-D26, cross-checking C93's arginine side chain atoms against D25/D26 coordinates.

Distances stay too far for D25 and D26 across all these checks, so no new contact there. I'm also confirming C94's side chain against D25, D26, D29, and D28, finding a valid contact only with D29, and reaffirming C90's contacts with D28, D29, and D32.

Continuing to rule out several other pairs — D32 with C83, D33 with C86, D35 with C86, D39 with C83 — all showing distances too large to count as contacts. I'm now moving on to check D43 against C73.

Also ruling out D46 with C70, and D49/D50 with C66 as too far apart. I'm turning to check whether chain C residues 52-63, which sit at higher x and y values, could overlap with chain D's range, and starting to look at C64's coordinates against D51.

Confirming D51 is out of range for those far C residues. I verify the D46-C73 contact distance calculation comes out to about 3.62, confirming it's a real interaction, and check D46-C72 similarly at 3.85. I then rule out D43 with C72/C73 and D46 with C69 based on distance, and start checking D45 against C72.

Continuing to rule out several more distant pairs — D45/C72, D44/C73, D40/C80, D37/C80/C84 — all too far apart. I revisit D32-C87 as marginal (~4.35-4.58) but confirmed separately through D36, and now I'm working out the D36-C87 distance to verify that contact too.

Confirming several other close contacts: C83-D35, D36-C83, C86-D32 all check out within range, and I'm now computing the C90-D29 distance.
